prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: transparent texture atlas for procedurally rendered fantasy board-game coastlines.
Input images are STYLE REFERENCES ONLY: the two original Small World board maps. Study their actual shorelines: dark earthy craggy plateau faces, watercolor/gouache texture, angular broken rock strata, tiny broken pale blue-white surf, consistent upper-left light. Draw NEW painted coast textures, not copies of any map region.
Create ONE landscape 1536x1024 PNG, genuinely transparent background, 2 columns and 3 rows of six SEPARATE horizontal coastal cliff-face strips, large transparent gutters, no text, labels or grid. Each cell contains a long narrow rock face (about 600px wide and 150px high), seen obliquely from above/front in the same illustrative style as the reference. Land is ABOVE each strip and water BELOW it but DO NOT paint broad land/water backgrounds. Each strip is an exposed rough rock face attached along its entire upper edge to a land plateau; top contour is broadly horizontal but irregular, bottom has short jagged broken rock edges, sides run off horizontally with abrupt cropped continuation (not tapered points). No oval/lens silhouettes or detached rock piles.
Top row: two charcoal umber / olive-earth coastal faces with subtle moss, one deeply cragged one stratified.
Middle row: two slate and deep brown coastal rock faces, one cool mountainous and one rugged forest coast.
Bottom row: two low ochre earth and weathered sandstone banks, sparse tiny sandy pockets and broken foam along the foot, still dark natural undercuts.
The exposed faces must have painterly irregular dark crevices, uneven angular stone ledges and subdued lighter ochre/gray highlights, large enough to read after scaling to only 15–25 pixels tall. Top rim only a very thin uneven earthy/mossy lip, no grass lawn, trees, bushes, buildings, fences or snow. Very restrained broken foam specks at the bottom, no blue water rectangle.
Absolutely no smooth gradients, retaining walls, bricks, masonry, vertical evenly spaced lines, barrels, boats, geometric panels, regular arc bands, giant pebbles or isolated decorative objects. The result must feel like part of the painted landmass from the references. True transparent alpha outside the six textures, not a checkerboard baked into the pixels.
note: The generator returned RGB artwork. Only six measured opaque rock-face rectangles are used as textures; display background, plateau caps and surrounding pixels are excluded by coastAtlasCatalog.js.
